STEP 1 - Scene: A plated meal of sautéed/stir-fried chicken pieces with broccoli and onion, alongside sliced zucchini and yellow squash. Photographed from above at a near-top-down angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: A square white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2 (treated as a round-equivalent dinner plate).

STEP 3 - Items:
- Zucchini (green skin, cut into wedges/half-moons)
- Yellow squash (cut into wedges)
- Chicken pieces (cooked, with some browning)
- Broccoli florets
- Onion/aromatics and a little sauce/oil residue

STEP 4 - Area (share of plate covered by food, about 50% total):
- Zucchini: ~15% (about 80 cm^2)
- Yellow squash: ~12% (about 64 cm^2)
- Chicken: ~15% (about 80 cm^2)
- Broccoli and onion: ~5% (about 27 cm^2)
- Sauce/oil residue: ~1%

STEP 5 - Volume (height estimates):
- Zucchini: 80 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 120 ml
- Yellow squash: 64 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 96 ml
- Chicken: 80 cm^2 x 1.2 cm ≈ 96 ml
- Broccoli/onion: 27 cm^2 x 1.5 cm ≈ 40 ml

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Zucchini: 120 ml x 0.6 ≈ 72 g
- Yellow squash: 96 ml x 0.6 ≈ 58 g
- Chicken: 96 ml x 0.95 ≈ 91 g
- Broccoli/onion: 40 ml x 0.6 ≈ 24 g

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Zucchini: 72 g x 17 kcal/100 g ≈ 12 kcal
- Yellow squash: 58 g x 16 kcal/100 g ≈ 9 kcal
- Chicken (cooked, stir-fried with some oil): 91 g x 190 kcal/100 g ≈ 173 kcal
- Broccoli/onion: 24 g x 35 kcal/100 g ≈ 8 kcal

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Total ≈ 245 g and ≈ 202 kcal. For a plate about half covered with a modest portion of chicken and vegetables, this is plausible. The chicken is the main energy source, and the vegetables are low in energy.
